findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and blocks it on every run
findings.body: The loop at lines 56-73 awaits `client.request` for each cancelled reminder inside a single try block. If the request throws for one reminder (for example SendGrid rejects a batch that was already sent or no longer exists), the exception skips every remaining reminder in `remindersToCancel`, and the catch only logs. Those reminders keep `cancelled: true` and are never cancelled or deleted. The query always returns the same ordered set, so the failing reminder is hit first again on the next 15-minute run and the rest stay stuck indefinitely. One bad row can therefore stop all cancellations, which is the same failure mode this PR is meant to fix. Each reminder should be cancelled in its own try/catch so that failures are isolated and the row is retried or logged individually.

findings.title: Cancellation of reminders due within the next hour is deferred and can still send
findings.body: For a cancelled booking, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called without `immediateDelete`, so it only sets `cancelled = true`. The actual SendGrid cancel happens in the cron job, which runs every 15 minutes and only picks up reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled 5 minutes before a reminder is due, and the cron last ran before the cancellation, the email can be sent before the next cron run actually cancels it. The same deferred path is used by the reschedule flow in bookings.tsx. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is inside the cron window at cancellation time should be cancelled immediately in SendGrid, and only the rest should be deferred.

findings.title: Paid booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled
findings.body: The `if (bookingToDelete.paid)` branch refunds the payment, marks the booking REJECTED and returns early at line ~464. The reminder cancellation block (`updatedBookings.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder)`) is placed after this return, so workflow reminders of paid bookings are never cancelled. Customers of paid, cancelled bookings still receive workflow reminders, which is the bug this PR claims to fix.

findings.title: Immediate-delete path cancels in SendGrid but leaves the reminder row marked as scheduled
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true and a referenceId exists, the function cancels the batch in SendGrid and returns without touching the `workflowReminder` row. The row keeps `scheduled: true` and its referenceId, and `cancelled` stays null. The cron job never picks it up for cancellation because it only selects `cancelled: true` rows, so the row lingers until its scheduledDate passes. This affects the reschedule path in handleNewBooking.ts, which passes `true`, and it is inconsistent with the cancel path, which sets the flag and expects the row to be removed later. The behaviour across the immediate and deferred modes should be made consistent.

findings.title: SMS cancellation has no retry and the DB row is only removed if Twilio cancel succeeds
findings.body: In `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, if `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, the function jumps to the catch and the reminder row is not deleted. Nothing retries the cancellation, unlike the email path, which at least has a cron. A transient Twilio error therefore lets the scheduled SMS for a cancelled or rescheduled booking go out. The same failure mode this PR fixes for email remains for SMS.

findings.title: No tests cover the new cancelled-reminder semantics or the cron cancellation path
findings.body: The PR changes the cancellation model (new `cancelled` column, deferred cancellation in the cron job, immediate vs deferred in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`), but no tests were added. Neither the cron cancellation loop, including its failure handling, nor the branching in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is covered. Those are exactly the paths where the reported bugs occur, so the regressions described above would not be caught.
